description: Classifying one channel's uploads as Shorts. A candidate is a video with a known duration (> 0) of at most 180 s; anything else is not a Short. With no candidates the Shorts list is not read. Otherwise a candidate is a Short iff it is in the list's newest page (`shortsList`, null when YouTube answers that the list doesn't exist). Only when the list is null and the platform can probe (`probe` present: videoId -> true, false, or null for an inconclusive answer or an error; an id missing from `probe` is an error) are the candidates probed instead, an inconclusive probe leaving the verdict unknown. `expected` maps each video to true, false, or null (unknown); `readsShortsList` and `probes` (in any order) say which requests are made. All of this applies only where the verdict is needed: a channel showing its uploads with its Shorts filter on `normal` (hide) or `shorts` (only). For any other channel no Shorts list is read and nothing is probed: a non-candidate is still not a Short, and a candidate is left unknown (so it gets no Shorts tag). When such a channel's filter later comes to need the verdict, the client reads the Shorts list for the uploads it already has (one request, none without a candidate) rather than fetching the uploads again; until then the Shorts filter holds the unknown ones back, as it does any unknown verdict.

cases.name: nothing short enough: the list is not read
unknown and zero durations are not candidates
candidates are judged by the list
180 s is a candidate, 181 s is not
an empty list means no Shorts
no list and no probe: no Shorts
a list wins over a probe
no list: candidates are probed instead
